findings.title: Central config (core/config.ini + get_default_options/apply_defaults) is dead: no consumer, and its values contradict the real defaults
findings.repro:
cd /Users/jmanning/hypertools && grep -rn 'get_default_options\|apply_defaults' hypertools/ --include='*.py' | grep -v __pycache__ | grep -v 'core/configurator\|core/__init__\|bound_args'  # -> no consumers
MPLBACKEND=Agg .venv/bin/python -c "
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
np.random.seed(0); X = np.random.randn(180, 4)
print('reduce default shape:', np.asarray(hyp.reduce(X)).shape)  # config.ini says ndims=3
import matplotlib; matplotlib.use('Agg')
fig = hyp.plot(np.cumsum(np.random.randn(120, 8), axis=0))
print('linewidth:', fig.gca().get_lines()[0].get_linewidth())  # config.ini says 1
"
findings.expected: Either config.ini values drive the actual defaults (reduce -> 3 dims, linewidth 1), or the module/config should not claim to be the central defaults mechanism
findings.actual: reduce default shape: (180, 4)  [not 3 dims]; actual linewidth: 1.5 | config.ini [plot] claims linewidth=1; marker: None | config claims style='.'; grep shows zero consumers

findings.title: Config values are returned as raw strings ('3', 'False', '0.7') that are unusable as kwargs and truthy-dangerous
findings.repro:
MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "
from hypertools.core import apply_defaults
import numpy as np
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
d = apply_defaults('cluster'); print(d, {k: type(v).__name__ for k, v in d.items()})
print('bool(verbose):', bool(d['verbose']))
KMeans(n_clusters=d['n_clusters']).fit(np.random.randn(50, 3))
"
findings.expected: Typed values (int 3, bool False, float 0.7) or documented string-only semantics with coercion helpers
findings.actual: {'n_clusters': '3', 'verbose': 'False'} {'n_clusters': 'str', 'verbose': 'str'}; bool(verbose): True; KMeans(n_clusters='3') -> InvalidParameterError : The 'n_clusters' parameter of KMeans must be an int in the range [1, inf). Got '3' instead. Also: dw.core.update_dict(dict(opts['plot']), {}, from_config=True) -> SyntaxError : invalid syntax (<string>, line 1)

findings.title: get_default_options(fname=) footguns: custom file silently REPLACES all hypertools defaults, nonexistent paths are silently ignored, sections are wholesale-replaced
findings.repro:
MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "
from hypertools.core import get_default_options
import tempfile, os
p = os.path.join(tempfile.mkdtemp(), 'c.ini'); open(p, 'w').write('[impute]\\nextra_opt = 1\\n')
print('missing file:', sorted(get_default_options(fname='/nonexistent/x.ini').keys())[:3], '(no error)')
c = get_default_options(fname=p)
print('[plot] after custom fname:', c['plot'])
print('[impute] after custom fname:', c['impute'])
"
findings.expected: Custom file layered ON TOP of hypertools+dw defaults (or a documented replacement contract); FileNotFoundError (or warning) for a missing fname; deep per-option merge
findings.actual: hypertools [plot] survives with custom fname: GONE (only dw defaults + custom file merged); nonexistent fname: silently returned sections ... (no error raised); dw default [impute]: {'model': \"'IterativeImputer'\"} -> after custom-file [impute]: {'extra_opt': '1'} (model key kept? False)

findings.title: RobustDict semantics are internally inconsistent: .get() bypasses the default, .copy() silently drops it, and the mutable default is aliased across lookups
findings.repro:
MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "
from hypertools.core.shared import RobustDict
rd = RobustDict({'a': 1}, __default_value__={})
rd['missing1']['polluted'] = True
print(rd['missing2'], rd['missing1'] is rd['missing2'])
rd2 = RobustDict({'a': 1}, __default_value__='DV')
print(rd2['zzz'], rd2.get('zzz'))
print(type(rd2.copy()).__name__)
rd2.copy()['zzz']
"
findings.expected: .get() honors the default; .copy() returns a RobustDict; a fresh default (e.g. copy) per missing lookup, or a documented immutability requirement
findings.actual: {'polluted': True} True | rd2['zzz'] -> DEFAULT ; rd2.get('zzz') -> None | copy() type: dict, then KeyError: 'zzz'

findings.title: Custom exceptions are not importable from the top-level hypertools namespace and are undocumented user-facing
findings.repro:
MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "
import hypertools as hyp
print(hasattr(hyp, 'HypertoolsError'), hasattr(hyp, 'HypertoolsIOError'), hasattr(hyp, 'HypertoolsBackendError'))
from hypertools import HypertoolsIOError
"
findings.expected: from hypertools import HypertoolsIOError works and is documented
findings.actual: False False False; ImportError: cannot import name 'HypertoolsIOError' from 'hypertools'

findings.title: Docstrings reference two different canonical exception paths; sources.py points at the deprecated _shared shim
findings.expected: All docstrings reference the same public path (hypertools.core.exceptions.* or a new top-level export)
findings.actual: lsl.py: 'hypertools.core.exceptions.HypertoolsIOError / If no matching stream is found'; sources.py: 'raises :class:`~hypertools._shared.exceptions.HypertoolsIOError`'; shim header: 'Moved to hypertools.core.exceptions (HyperTools 1.0 refactor). Kept as a shim'

findings.title: unpack_model silently ignores 'params' when both 'params' and 'kwargs' are present in a dict spec
findings.repro:
MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -W error::DeprecationWarning -c "
from hypertools.core.shared import unpack_model
from sklearn.decomposition import PCA
print(unpack_model({'model': 'PCA', 'params': {'n_components': 4}, 'kwargs': {'n_components': 9}}, valid=[PCA]))
print(unpack_model({'mdoel': 'PCA'}, valid=[PCA]))
"
findings.expected: A warning (or error) that 'params' conflicts with 'kwargs' and is being ignored; a clear error for dicts lacking a 'model' key
findings.actual: {'model': <class 'sklearn.decomposition._pca.PCA'>, 'params': {'n_components': 4}, 'kwargs': {'n_components': 9}, 'args': []} with no warning raised (-W error did not trip); {'mdoel': 'PCA'} passed through unchanged

findings.title: unpack_model error messages leak raw reprs (memory addresses) and give no guidance; class-vs-instance validation is asymmetric
findings.expected: Error names the offending spec, the accepted spec forms (string among valid names / class or instance of parent_class / dict with 'model'), e.g. 'NotAModel instance is not a BaseEstimator; pass a class/instance of ... or one of [...]'
findings.actual: 1: unknown model: <__main__.NotAModel object at 0x100647d10> | 2: unknown model: <class 'sklearn.decomposition._pca.PCA'> | 3: 'PCA' PCA()  (string and instance pass through where the class raised)

findings.title: hypertools.config is a misnomer holding only __version__, leaks importlib's 'version' function, and carries dead Python<3.8 fallback code
findings.repro:
MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "
import hypertools.config as c
print([a for a in dir(c) if not a.startswith('_')])
print(c.version)
print(c.__version__)
"
findings.expected: Module exposes only __version__ (del version after use, or use 'from importlib.metadata import version as _version'); no <3.8 fallback in a >=3.10 package

findings.title: Default n_clusters differs by entry point: hyp.cluster() -> 3 but hyp.plot(cluster='KMeans') -> 5 (three competing default sources)
findings.expected: Same default k for the same spec on both entry points
findings.actual: hyp.cluster(X) unique labels: 3 | hyp.plot(X, '.', cluster='KMeans') distinct colors: 5 | hyp.cluster(X, cluster='KMeans') unique labels: 3

findings.title: set_interactive_backend accepts an invalid backend name silently; HypertoolsBackendError only surfaces at the first interactive plot
findings.repro:
MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
hyp.set_interactive_backend('bogus_backend_xyz')  # no error here
print('set silently OK')
hyp.plot(np.random.randn(30, 3), interactive=True)
"
findings.expected: Immediate error/warning naming the unknown backend at set time
findings.actual: set silently OK; then on plot: HypertoolsBackendError : Failed to switch the plotting backend to bogus_backend_xyz. You may be missing required dependencies, or this backend may not be available for your system
